A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, algorithms, figures, references, and complete Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original DP-SGD auditing experiments in Section 6.2 and Appendix D.3, plus ORA–AORA simulations on Count-in-Sets in Appendix E.3.2.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical studies and adds an ORA–AORA comparison on single-step DP-SGD in Section 6.3 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Adaptive ORA, including revealing previously guessed bits and permitting adaptive guessing order, already appears in v2 Definition E.3. v3 evaluates the existing approach on DP-SGD without substantively changing the proposed auditing procedures.

E1.justification: The synthetic gradient-canary DP-SGD task and Count-in-Sets simulations are retained. The new DP-SGD comparison changes steps, sampling, and guessing settings within existing task coverage; it introduces no new dataset or application domain.

E2.justification: v3 adds AORA alongside ORA in the DP-SGD comparison in Figure 3. In v2, the empirical ORA–AORA comparison was confined to Count-in-Sets, while the DP-SGD plots evaluated ORA.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 adds a single-step, full-batch DP-SGD protocol using maximum-likelihood guessers with privacy-loss threshold τ=1. The existing Section 6.2 protocol retains 100 steps, sampling rate 0.1, and a fixed number of guesses.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds an analysis of whether AORA's advantage persists with noise and a finite guessing threshold as elements per coordinate increase. Existing abstention, privacy-parameter, and Count-in-Sets sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Reported repetitions increase from 100 to 200 for the main DP-SGD experiments and from 50 to 100 for the Count-in-Sets simulation. Standard-error reporting and the 95% privacy-bound confidence convention are retained.

E6.justification: Existing empirical curves are updated: Section 6.2's one-element-per-coordinate mean bound changes from 0.45±0.02 to 0.49±0.01. New Figure 3 reports higher AORA bounds than ORA under its single-step protocol, with the advantage persisting as interference increases. This adds evidence under a new protocol rather than demonstrating a revised method's same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The efficacy and asymptotic-tightness results, counterexamples, and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged, including AORA's validity proof. The Count-in-Sets definition moves from Definition D.4 to Definition 6.1 with a grouping clarification, rather than a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the characterization of three auditing gaps, tightness conditions, and mitigation through multiple canaries and adaptivity. Explicitly highlighting AORA and adding a conclusion foreground existing claims; the new experiment supplies additional support.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 newly explains how revealed bits enable later confident guesses despite interference in noisy DP-SGD. v3 also refines the discussion of applicability to approximate DP and explains the distinction between small interference from random high-dimensional gradients and its elimination by Dirac canaries.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new comparison's full-batch configuration, τ=1 threshold, and likelihood calculations conditioned on previously revealed bits for AORA. The existing code-access link is retained.

R1.justification: v3 removes citations to Bassily et al.'s Coupled-worlds privacy and Barber–Duchi's Privacy and statistical risk along with the associated related-work paragraph. It also refines the description of f-DP auditing and Xiang et al.; the main novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: v3 revises several introductory and explanatory paragraphs, standardizes 'coordinate' terminology, moves the Count-in-Sets definition into the main text, and adds Sections 6.3 and 7. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 3, enlarges and restyles existing plots, expands several captions, and relocates Figures 1–2 within the experimental discussion. Existing appendix figures are retained and renumbered; there is no wholesale layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v2's empirical support for AORA was limited to noiseless Count-in-Sets; v3 adds a controlled noisy DP-SGD comparison in Section 6.3. Increased repetitions and clearer explanations also strengthen the paper. These gains are limited because the new comparison remains a simplified single-step canary experiment, with comprehensive realistic evaluation still left for future work.
